page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, delivering 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The processor package features 54 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and support for hardware instructions including AVX-512 with VNNI, VAES, and SHA extensions. Memory density is the primary feature of this instance, delivering 256 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, translating to an expansive 32 GB of memory per core. Bundled local storage is provided by a 237 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 5 Gbps baseline network capacity.

Benchmark results reflect stable mid-tier compute performance alongside dependable memory throughput. Synthetic CPU assessments register a Geekbench single-core score of 1647.0 and multi-core score of 6078.0, matching the PassMark CPU evaluation of 11305.6. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 58.31 GB/sec for read operations and 41.67 GB/sec for writes, scaling up to 414.09 GB/sec for cached 16 KB read workloads. High-throughput data processing is substantiated by Redis SET performance, reaching 7.93 million operations per second. However, compute-bound multithreaded tasks reveal architectural limits, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the lower quartile and 7B model prompt processing registering a relatively weak 16.29 tokens per second.

From an infrastructure and efficiency perspective, x2iedn.2xlarge provides high memory-to-vCPU allocation, prioritizing RAM capacity over raw thread scaling. The instance offers strong resource density for configurations that demand significant memory footprints without paying for superfluous virtual cores. This hardware combination makes the instance well suited for large in-memory databases, caching tiers like Redis, enterprise ERP environments, real-time analytics engines, and memory-bound ETL batch workflows.
description: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, the configuration supplies 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs alongside 54 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 support. With 256 GB of DDR4-3000 memory, the machine delivers a substantial 32 GB of RAM per vCPU, complemented by an integrated 237 GB NVMe SSD and a 5 Gbps network interface. Synthetic evaluations demonstrate balanced compute performance, including a PassMark CPU score of 11305.6, large-block read memory bandwidth of 58.31 GB/sec, and 7.93 million Redis SET operations per second. While multi-threaded compression performance is lower due to the 8-vCPU ceiling, the instance is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, in-memory databases, and large-scale caching services.
